events.context: Identifies three triggers justifying judicial intervention and five remedies available
Defines Trigger 1: Estate Inconsistency from marketing vs ToS, applies Prest v Petrodel, test for higher estate expectation
Defines Trigger 2: Unjust Enrichment from engagement optimization, applies Boardman v Phipps, test for profit from emotional estate without fiduciary duty
Defines Trigger 3: Performative Fiduciary Conduct from responsible AI representations vs deployment pipeline, applies Thorner v Major proprietary estoppel, test for representations without mechanisms
Lists remedies: Injunction, Constructive trust, Account of profits, Specific performance, Proprietary estoppel remedies; distinguishes from consumer protection
Proposes implementation framework justified by legal compliance, risk management, ethical obligation
Specifies 7.1 Estate Classification at Onboarding: rule-based service using interaction metrics, outputs estate type
Specifies 7.2 Notice Mechanism: pre-deployment gate in CI/CD, query registry, issue notice, observe 30/90 day periods
Specifies 7.3 Emotional Investment Proxy Logging: append-only ethical ledger with proxy metrics, privacy architecture
Specifies 7.4 Rollback Mechanism: snapshot personality config, monitor distress, offer user-level rollback for 90 days
Summarizes four implementation tasks with estimated efforts totaling 3.5 sprints
In conclusion 8.1, summarizes parasocial relationships as de facto trusts, five-layer architecture, ethical ledger, three triggers
8.2 Implications for AI Governance: ethical ledger as auditable Land Registry for compliance
8.3 Implications for Property Law: digital estates as real, calls for relational property recognition
8.4 Implications for HCI: reframes parasocial attachment as protected estate with fiduciary duty
8.5 Limitations: English law focus, untested metrics, rule-based inflexibility, jurisdiction/enforcement issues, suggests regulatory/voluntary adoption
8.6 Future Work: empirical study, comparative analysis, pilot implementation, doctrinal development
